title: Cross browser check with web standards
when: The user wants a page or app checked so it works in all current browser engines, using standards and fallbacks, not hacks.
inputs: the oldest devices the audience uses
prompt:
Goal: A compatibility report listing newer features in use, how each degrades, and fixes so the core task works in every current engine.
Steps:
1. Inventory features: CSS (:has(), container queries, nesting, subgrid, color-mix, dvh), JS (structuredClone, top level await, Array.prototype.at), HTML (dialog, popover, date and color inputs).
2. Mark each as widely available, newly available or limited, and note its fallback.
3. CSS fallbacks: safe value first, new value second (height: 100vh; height: 100dvh); risky blocks inside @supports.
4. JS detection: test the feature itself ("showModal" in HTMLDialogElement.prototype) and keep content visible if a module fails.
5. Known differences: date input formats, autoplay rules, form validation bubbles, smooth scrolling, mobile toolbar height.
6. Test in the three main engines plus one phone; note engine and version per issue.
Quality bar:
- Core content and main action work everywhere.
- Enhancements fail quietly.
- No user agent sniffing.
Pitfalls:
- Prefixed hacks without the standard property.
- Testing in one engine only.
- Detecting features from the user agent string.
Verify:
- [ ] Feature inventory with status.
- [ ] Fallbacks or @supports present.
- [ ] JS detection checked.
- [ ] Engines tested are listed.
Output: compat-report.md with the feature table and the issues.

examples.output: :has() used for menu state, no fallback; dialog used without showModal check; fixes listed per feature
